questions.q: Pablo Antonio is most famous for the design of which university campus, considered the largest ensemble of Art Deco architecture in Manila?
questions.n: The FEU campus in Manila is Antonio's masterpiece, featuring a consistent Art Deco theme across its main buildings.

questions.q: Pablo Antonio's design philosophy was 'Function before Elegance.' This was a departure from which style favored by his predecessors like Toledo?
questions.n: Neoclassicism prioritized formal symmetry and classical ornamentation, which Antonio simplified in favor of clean, functional lines.

questions.q: Which specific building type did Pablo Antonio revolutionize in the 1930s and 40s, designing famous examples like the Ideal, Life, and Galaxy?
questions.n: Antonio was the premier architect for grand Art Deco cinemas, which became icons of Manila's pre-war urban life.

questions.q: In his residential designs, Pablo Antonio was a pioneer in using which climate-responsive feature to handle the Philippine heat?
questions.n: Antonio used wide eaves, louvers, and strategic window placements to maximize airflow and minimize solar heat gain.

questions.q: True or False: Pablo Antonio was posthumously conferred the title of National Artist for Architecture in 1976.
questions.n: He was the second architect to receive this honor, recognized for his significant role in the development of Philippine Modernism.

questions.q: Which specific hall at the Far Eastern University campus is considered the main administrative building and a prime example of Antonio's Art Deco style?
questions.n: Named after the university's founder, this building serves as the centerpiece of the Art Deco ensemble.

questions.q: Pablo Antonio often used 'Streamline Moderne' elements in his designs. Which of these is a characteristic of that style?
o: Curving forms, long horizontal lines, and nautical elements
Heavy, ornate carvings of classical deities
questions.n: Streamline Moderne focused on aerodynamic shapes and horizontal emphasis to suggest speed and modernity.

questions.q: In designing the FEU Auditorium, how did Antonio address the challenge of acoustics and visibility without modern electronic aids?
o: By incorporating a wide, fan-shaped plan
By using a flat, square room layout
By lining the walls with heavy velvet curtains only
By building the auditorium entirely underground
questions.n: The fan shape ensures better sightlines and directs sound more effectively toward the audience.

questions.q: Pablo Antonio designed the Manila Railroad Company's main terminal. What is this building called today?
questions.n: Antonio designed the pre-war expansion and modernization of this vital transportation hub.

questions.q: Antonio's 'Function before Elegance' maxim suggests that a building's beauty should arise from:
o: Its practical utility and structural logic
How closely it mimics ancient Roman temples
The complexity of its hidden riddles
The amount of gold leaf applied to the facade
questions.n: He believed that if a building worked perfectly for its purpose, it would naturally possess an inherent elegance.

questions.q: Which of these materials did Pablo Antonio favor for his Art Deco interiors, often seen in the staircases of FEU?
o: Carved narra wood in Baroque style
questions.n: Antonio used these materials to create durable, modern, and visually striking geometric transitions in his buildings.

questions.q: True or False: Pablo Antonio was known for being an introvert who avoided the social limelight, focusing almost entirely on his work.
questions.n: Unlike some of his more social peers, Antonio was known for his quiet dedication and focus on his architectural practice.

questions.q: What happened to many of Pablo Antonio's famous theater designs, such as the Ideal Theater, after World War II and the subsequent urban decay of Manila?
o: They were converted into government offices
They were preserved as National Landmarks
Many were demolished or fell into severe disrepair
They were moved brick-by-brick to Las Casas Filipinas de Acuzar
questions.n: The loss of buildings like the Ideal Theater is considered a major blow to Manila's architectural heritage.

questions.q: In his residential work, Pablo Antonio's own home is a testament to his style. Where is the Pablo Antonio Residence located?
questions.n: His residence in Pasay is now a heritage site and a showcase of his tropical modernist principles.

questions.q: Which of these awards did Pablo Antonio receive for his contributions to the city of Manila in 1952?
o: Patnubay ng Sining at Kalinangan Award
questions.n: He was recognized early on for his immense impact on the visual and architectural identity of the city.

questions.q: Pablo Antonio is often credited with introducing a specific sub-style of Art Deco to the Philippines characterized by smooth surfaces and curved corners. What is this style?
questions.n: This style emphasized aerodynamic curves and horizontal lines, reflecting the era's fascination with speed and machines.

questions.q: In the FEU Nicanor Reyes Hall, Antonio used which geometric element prominently in the staircases and railings?
o: Repeating horizontal bars and clean angles
questions.n: The use of strong horizontal lines and geometric simplicity is a hallmark of the Art Deco movement in his work.

questions.q: Which of these famous pre-war structures designed by Pablo Antonio was a major commercial hub in the heart of Manila?
questions.n: Located on Avenida Rizal, this cinema was a premier commercial landmark and a showcase of Antonio's Art Deco mastery.

questions.q: Antonio's residential designs often featured 'ventanillas' and wide eaves. What was the primary functional goal of these features?
o: To increase the building's structural weight
To facilitate passive cooling and sun shading
To serve as decorative framing for photos
questions.n: By allowing air to flow through the floor level and shading walls from the sun, he adapted modernism for the tropics.

questions.q: True or False: Pablo Antonio was the first architect to be named a National Artist of the Philippines.
questions.n: Antonio was the second architect to receive the title; Juan Nakpil was the first.

questions.q: The FEU Auditorium designed by Antonio is noted for its acoustic quality. Which architectural feature most contributes to this?
o: The use of heavy lead lining in the walls
The fan-shaped floor plan and sloped seating
Covering all surfaces in thick carpet
questions.n: This geometry allows sound to travel clearly from the stage to the back of the house without echoes.

questions.q: Which of these materials was frequently used by Antonio for the sleek, polished surfaces found in his Art Deco interiors?
questions.n: Terrazzo provided a smooth, durable, and modern finish that allowed for the geometric patterns typical of his work.

questions.q: What was Antonio's stance on the use of ornamentation in architecture?
o: It should be the primary focus of every design
It should be integrated into the form and serve a purpose
He only used ornaments imported from Europe
He believed all buildings should be completely plain blocks
questions.n: Antonio believed that beauty should come from the building's logic and utility, not from 'pasted-on' decorations.

questions.q: The Manila Railroad Company terminal expansion (Tutuban) by Antonio is significant because it showed his ability to modernize what?
questions.n: His work on Tutuban modernized the experience of travel, bringing a sleek, efficient look to the railway.

questions.q: Pablo Antonio's home in Pasay City is currently used as what?
o: A heritage site and restaurant/event space
questions.n: The home is preserved as a museum of his style and a venue that celebrates his architectural legacy.

questions.q: In the context of his work at FEU, how did Antonio's design handle the transition between the interior and exterior spaces to manage the tropical climate?
o: By building all structures below the water table
By sealing the buildings with air-tight glass panels
By using thick, windowless concrete walls
By incorporating wide open corridors and permeable facades
questions.n: These features allow for natural cross-ventilation, reducing the need for mechanical cooling in a tropical setting.

questions.q: The 'Galaxy Theater' was another of Antonio's masterpieces. What happened to this building that serves as a lesson in Philippine architectural heritage?
o: It was demolished to give way to a shopping mall
It was converted into a public library
It was meticulously restored to its 1930s glory
It remains as an abandoned, but protected, shell
questions.n: The loss of the Galaxy is a primary example of how commercial interests often override heritage preservation in urban areas.

questions.q: Pablo Antonio used 'Louvers' extensively in his residential designs. What is the primary architectural purpose of a louver?
o: To reflect sound waves back into a room
To act as a secret passage between rooms
To allow air and light in while keeping rain and direct sun out
To increase the structural load-bearing capacity of a wall
questions.n: Louvers consist of angled slats that facilitate ventilation while providing shade and protection from the elements.

questions.q: True or False: Before his career in architecture, Pablo Antonio worked as a draftsman in the Bureau of Public Works (BPW).
questions.n: Like many of his contemporaries, he gained foundational experience in the government's design office before rising to fame.

questions.q: Which specific geometric shape is most associated with the 'Art Deco' style that Antonio mastered, particularly in his facade designs?
questions.n: These geometric patterns are signature elements of the Art Deco movement, representing modern energy and dynamism.

questions.q: Antonio's 'White Cross Sanatorium' in San Juan utilized which specific layout to aid in the recovery of patients?
o: A replica of a traditional European castle
A circular maze to keep patients from leaving
A dense, multi-story tower with small windows
A linear, spread-out plan to maximize sunlight and breeze
questions.n: The design focused on the 'healing' properties of the environment, using a plan that allowed every room to be well-ventilated.

questions.q: The use of 'Terrazzo' in Antonio's buildings was not just for aesthetics but also for 'Durability.' What makes terrazzo a durable choice for high-traffic public areas?
o: It requires daily waxing with rare oils to stay intact
It is a seamless, hard-wearing surface made of stone chips and cement
It is made of recycled paper and glue
It is soft and cushions the impact of footsteps
questions.n: Its resistance to wear and ease of cleaning make it ideal for university hallways and theater lobbies.

questions.q: Which of these concepts describes Antonio's approach to the 'Media Agua' (awning) in his modern buildings?
o: Replacing them with modern digital screens
Transforming them into sleek, horizontal concrete slabs
Using only nipa palm for a 'native' look
Eliminating them to make the building look like a flat box
questions.n: He took a traditional element and modernized it into a structural feature that provided shade without looking 'old-fashioned'.

questions.q: Antonio's work on the 'Manila Pole Club' highlighted his skill in designing for which specific social activity?
questions.n: The design needed to reflect both the prestige of the club and the functional requirements of the sport and its observers.

questions.q: True or False: Pablo Antonio's sons also became prominent architects, continuing his legacy and preserving his archives.
questions.n: His family, particularly his son Pablo Antonio Jr., has been instrumental in maintaining his heritage and the Pasay residence.

questions.q: Pablo Antonio is a celebrated National Artist. In which city can you find his most famous concentrated collection of Art Deco buildings at a university campus?
questions.n: The Far Eastern University (FEU) campus in Manila is the primary site for his iconic Art Deco designs.

questions.q: Antonio's 'Function before Elegance' philosophy means that he believed a building's beauty should primarily come from its:
o: Usefulness and how well it works
Number of statues on the roof
questions.n: He believed that a building designed perfectly for its purpose would be naturally beautiful.

questions.q: Which of these is a common feature of 'Streamline Moderne', the sub-style of Art Deco that Antonio often used?
o: Curved corners and long horizontal lines
questions.n: This style was inspired by the look of modern ships and trains to suggest speed and efficiency.

questions.q: Antonio designed many famous movie theaters. Why were these 'cinemas' so important to his career?
o: They were used as secret government bunkers
They were the only buildings he ever designed
He owned all the theaters he designed
They allowed him to experiment with grand, modern Art Deco facades
questions.n: Theaters like the Ideal and Life were the high-profile 'billboards' for his modern architectural ideas.

questions.q: In his tropical designs, Antonio used 'wide eaves.' What do these eaves protect the building from?
o: Direct sunlight and heavy tropical rain
questions.n: By extending the roof over the windows, he kept the interior cool and dry without closing the building up.

questions.q: What material did Antonio favor for durable, polished floors in public buildings like the FEU campus?
questions.n: Terrazzo is extremely durable and can be polished to a high shine, making it perfect for high-traffic schools.

questions.q: The 'Nicanor Reyes Hall' at FEU is named after the university's founder. What is this building's main role?
o: A dormitory for international students only
The main administrative and classroom building
questions.n: It serves as the heart of the campus and is a primary example of Antonio's grand style.

questions.q: True or False: Pablo Antonio's work helped move Philippine architecture away from the 'copying' of old Western styles like Neoclassicism.
questions.n: He was a pioneer of the Modernist movement which sought a new, functional language for the 20th century.

questions.q: When Antonio designed the White Cross Sanatorium, he spread the buildings out. Why was this 'spread out' plan helpful for patients?
o: To hide the building from the main road
To provide maximum fresh air and natural light
Because they ran out of concrete to build a tall tower
To make the nurses walk more for exercise
questions.n: Sanatoriums treated diseases like TB, which required clean air and sunlight to help patients heal.

questions.q: Pablo Antonio was awarded the title of 'National Artist.' Is this the highest honor a Filipino artist can receive?
o: No, it is just a participation trophy
No, there is a 'Galaxy Artist' award that is higher
Yes, it is the highest state recognition for Filipino artists
It is an award only for painters, not architects
questions.n: The Order of National Artists is the supreme award for significant cultural contributions to the nation.
